title: Happy New Year (My Goals Going Into 2026)

content.text:
I have a few different goals in mind for 2026. My main goal is going to be studying for and getting into a grad program for quantum gravity / black hole information. I have a fair amount of books building up to the subject and have ordered quite a few more that are yet to arrive. My educational background includes a B.S. in Aerospace Engineering from TAMU in 2022 and a B.S. in biophysics I'll be receiving this spring, so while I am not starting completely from scratch, I still have a lot of work to do in order to understand any in depth work in the field meaningfully. I generated a list of some 75 books and papers that I would like to read to get a solid foundational understanding of the topics. I'm not sure that reading all of them in 2026 is a reasonable and realistic goal, but I would like to read a good amount every day and document my learning journey. Some of the big books on my list are:

  -Spacetime and Geometry by Sean Carroll
  -General Relativity by Robert Wald
  -An Introduction to Quantum Field Theory by Peskin and Schroeder
  -Quantum Fields in Curved Space by Birrell and Davies
  -Quantum Field Theory in Curved Spacetime and Black Hole Thermodynamics by Robert Wald
  -A First Course in String Theory by Barton Zweibach
  -Conformal Field Theory by Di Francesco, Mathieu, and Senechal
  -AdS/CFT Duality User Guide by Makoto Natsuume

If I were to open up any of these books right now I likely would get stuck in a matter of minutes. I really need to build up my knowledge of tensor calculus, statistical mechanics, and quantum mechanics before I even approach these. To that end I have a great many more books laid out from foundational mathematics to advanced physics. I want to start on firm ground so I've decided my first book of 2026 will be 'Mathematical Methods in the Physical Sciences' by Mary L. Boas. While I have already encountered many of the topics in this textbook, my hope is that this book will add a much greater depth to my knowledge of core mathematical topics as it is renowned for its rigor and depth.

So what of my other goals? I'd say the rest of my goals are pretty cookie cutter, I'd like to eat healthier and exercise more. There is a fitness center at LANL that is free for employees, so I really have no excuses to be sedentary this year. I'm also surrounded by beautiful mountains so I really just need to find something to do until it gets warm enough to start hiking again. As for eating healthier, I think all together I do a decent job of prepping meals and not making food that's super unhealthy, this goal will mainly focus on eating out less and making lunch instead of eating at the work cafeteria every day.

I've often felt like I'm just around the corner from some huge life transition where I will magically become a much better person both intellectually and health wise, my broadest goal of 2026 is to not enter 2027 feeling like that. Good luck to everyone else with their goals and I hope 2026 treats you well.
